description: VILLASframework is a model listed in Open Energy Platform model and framework factsheets, a public register of energy-system model and framework factsheets under the section "Models", published or maintained by RWTH Aachen. VILLASframework is a toolset for local and geographically distributed real-time co-simulation. Real-time simulators are already used extensively for academic research as well as industrial applications in electrical power networks. The primary application of real-time simulators is in the area of hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) simulation. Coverage: not restricted to one place on the factsheet. Methodical focus: co-simulation, real-time. Software: C++. The listed link gives the source code or documentation; nothing was downloaded or run. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is Apache license 2.0. Caveats: this record was written from the Open Energy Platform factsheet only, so the code, documentation and any publication it links were not opened, their current availability was not checked, and the factsheet may lag the project. It can support energy-system planning and scenario studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-oep-factsheet-catalogue.

outputs: VILLAS is framework for coupling test beds and real-time simulators between geographically distributed laboratories. The development of VILLAS is mainly driven by RWTH Aachen University and was originally designed here for geographically distributed real-time simulation of electrical networks, but can also be used without restrictions for simulation in other domains as well as multi-physical systems. The framework consists of several independent components, which can be combined according to requirements and needed functions. Central is VILLASnode as interface for the coupling between the involved components. It enables real-time data exchange via various protocols and data formats. In addition, VILLASweb provides a web-based user interface with which scenarios, user groups, laboratory infrastructure and measurement results can be managed. The execution of experiments can be monitored and controlled by means of a freely programmable virtual control room. For this purpose, real-time data can be transferred directly to the web-based control room via the VILLASnode interface. The configuration, inventory and control of the involved laboratory infrastructure is realized via the VILLAScontroller, which exchanges the current status as well as control commands and configurations between the virtual control room and the laboratory infrastructure. The modular structure of the framework allows easy extensibility with new interfaces, protocols and data formats. This is supported by the open development approach, which makes the framework fully available as open source software under the Apache 2.0 license to external users, allowing them to collaborate on the common code base.
